To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
solar power can replace coal mining jobs in areas suitable for PV deployment, but wind power is not suitable to replace coal mining jobs because wind power has limited resource availability.

(1) several GWs of local solar or wind capacity are required in each coal-mining area to transition all miners to renewables; (2) while solar has more suitable resource availability than wind in coal-mining areas, these resources do not exist everywhere; and (3), countries would have to significantly scale-up their solar capacity to transition all coal-miners in areas suitable for renewables.
solar power has greater techno-economic suitability than wind power to replace coal mining jobs, and solar power has greater resource suitability than wind power in coal mining areas.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the potential for renewable energy to create jobs in areas where coal is mined.
the techno-economic feasibility of transitioning coal miners to solar and wind jobs.
the potential for solar and wind jobs to replace coal mining jobs in the countries with the largest number of coal miners.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the techno-economic resource suitability for replacing coal miners in China, India, Australia, and the US is greater for solar than wind power, and that the scale of renewable development required to replace coal miners is large.
solar and wind power have the potential to transition coal miners, but this potential is limited in some countries and regions, and would require significant deployment of solar/wind capacity.
solar and wind power are not suitable for replacing coal mining workers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
solar and wind have greater techno-economic resource potential than wind for replacing local coal jobs.
the transition of local coal miners to solar and wind jobs will not be easy.
solar has greater techno-economic and resource suitability than wind to replace coal mining jobs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
solar and wind power can replace local coal mining jobs, but the scale of deployment required is substantial.
coal miners are likely to be left behind as coal jobs disappear, unless they are able to migrate or governments invest heavily in solar/wind deployment.
coal miners cannot transition to solar/wild jobs everywhere and in large enough numbers to replace all coal mining jobs in the near-term.
